World rule: surfaces.road ('mud' pattern) renders as long parallel plank or wood-grain streaks along x. It needs a blotchy, non-directional mud pattern with darker wet patches, or it will always read as a wooden deck.

World rule: The street tile's walking edge (|z| 4-6) is drawn as a distinct straight band with its own repeating round pattern, which reads as a pavement or sidewalk even though pavement is null. World rule: Trees rule: add hard geometry rules. No foliage sphere clusters sitting centred on top of a single trunk; no conifer cones stacked on a single axis; at least 40% of each crown's mass offset to one side of the trunk; visible gaps between foliage clumps; at least one bare or dead branch per tree.

World rule: trees: forbid stacked cones for conifers and a single cluster of spheres on a pole for broadleaf crowns. Require foliage as separated, offset clumps on visible bare branches with at least one dead limb, since 'never use centred lollipop crowns' alone was not enough.

Give the shorter pine a kinked trunk, unequal branch lengths and a dominant lateral foliage mass; retain their specified positions without making them a matched pair. / Birch: lean the trunk 0.3 rad toward the road. Split it into 2 forked leaders that diverge by more than 0.8 rad. Replace the sphere cloud with 3–4 small separate foliage clumps (0.9–1.4 m flattened boxes or icosahedron-like spheres) placed at the branch tips with visible gaps and bare branch between them. Push the largest mass 1.2 m off the trunk axis on one side and add 2 bare dead twigs on top. Pine: shift the cones so their centres step 0.4–0.6 m sideways each tier. Make one tier on the windward side missing (bare trunk showing) and the leeward side heavy. Lean the trunk 0.25 rad, crop the top cone off-centre, and add a snapped dead branch. Replace the round shrub with a ragged 3-box scrub clump. / Birch: lean the trunk 15-20 degrees and split it into two unequal forks. Hang 3-4 small, separated foliage clumps (0.8-1.4 m) off the ends of bare branches, leaving gaps and one dead bare limb. Pine: replace the stacked cones with 3-4 flattened, offset foliage slabs (wide boxes/cones squashed to 0.6 m tall) sticking out to one side at different heights. Bend the trunk with one kink, leave the top bare and snapped, and keep a broken lower branch stub.
